hchart Function

Source: vignettes/hchart.Rmd
hchart.Rmd

This a generic function, this means you can chart various R like numeric, histograms, character, factor, ts on the fly. The resulting chart is a highchart object so you can keep modifying with the implemented API.

Data Frames

This function works like qplot: You pass the data, choose the type of chart and then define the aesthetics for each variable.

library(highcharter)
library(dplyr)

data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")
data(diamonds, economics_long, package = "ggplot2")

hchart(
  penguins,
  "scatter",
  hcaes(x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm, group = species)
)
penguins2 <- penguins |>
  count(species, island) |>
  glimpse()
## Rows: 5
## Columns: 3
## $ species <fct> Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Chinstrap, Gentoo
## $ island  <fct> Biscoe, Dream, Torgersen, Dream, Biscoe
## $ n       <int> 44, 56, 52, 68, 124
hchart(penguins2, "column", hcaes(x = island, y = n, group = species))

Check automatically if the x column is date class:

economics_long2 <- economics_long |>
  filter(variable %in% c("pop", "uempmed", "unemploy"))

hchart(economics_long2, "line", hcaes(x = date, y = value01, group = variable))

Numeric & Histograms 

x <- diamonds$price
hchart(x)

Densities 

hchart(density(x), type = "area", color = "#B71C1C", name = "Price")

Precomputed histograms

Pass a histogram object when you want R to choose the breaks before charting. The bin boundaries and counts are preserved.

hchart(hist(diamonds$price, breaks = 30, plot = FALSE), name = "Diamond prices")

Character & Factor 

x <- diamonds$cut
hchart(x, type = "column")

Time Series 

hchart(LakeHuron, name = "Level") |>
  hc_title(text = "Level of Lake Huron 1875–1972")

Seasonal Decomposition of Time Series by Loess 

x <- stl(log(AirPassengers), "per")
hchart(x)

Forecast package

The legend distinguishes the observed series from the forecast. Prediction intervals are linked to the forecast series. Supply name to label the subject; the chart adds the observed/forecast suffixes.

library(forecast)

x <- forecast(ets(USAccDeaths), h = 48, level = 95)
hchart(x)

Exponential-smoothing components

An ets model shows its observed values and fitted level, slope or seasonal states in aligned panels. To show future values instead, pass the model to forecast() and chart the resulting forecast object.

hchart(forecast::ets(AirPassengers))

Multivariate Time series 

x <- cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths)
hchart(x)

Seasonal decomposition

The four panels share a time axis and show the observed series, seasonality, trend and remainder. Gaps at the ends of the trend are part of the fitted decomposition.

hchart(stats::decompose(AirPassengers, type = "multiplicative"))

Seasonal adjustment with X-13

With the optional seasonal package installed, compare the original monthly series with the X-13-adjusted series on the same scale. Labels mark the outliers reported by the model at the adjusted value, as in plot(fit) (e.g., AO for an additive outlier or LS for a level shift).

fit <- seasonal::seas(AirPassengers)
hchart(fit)

Autocovariance & Autocorrelation 

changes <- diff(AirPassengers)
hchart(acf(changes, plot = FALSE))
hchart(pacf(changes, plot = FALSE))

Igraph package 

library(igraph)
N <- 40

net <- sample_gnp(N, p = 2 / N)
wc <- cluster_walktrap(net)

V(net)$label <- seq(N)
V(net)$name <- paste("I'm #", seq(N))
V(net)$page_rank <- round(page_rank(net)$vector, 2)
V(net)$betweenness <- round(betweenness(net), 2)
V(net)$degree <- degree(net)
V(net)$size <- V(net)$degree
V(net)$comm <- as.vector(membership(wc))
V(net)$color <- colorize(membership(wc))

hchart(net, layout = layout_with_fr)

Survival Package

Survival models can be charted.

library(survival)

data(cancer, package = "survival")

lung <- dplyr::mutate(cancer, sex = ifelse(sex == 1, "Male", "Female"))

fit <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ sex, data = cancer)

hchart(fit, ranges = TRUE)

Quantmod package

The highstock extension is used to chart xts and xts ohlc classes from the quantmod package.

library(quantmod)

data(sample_matrix, package = "xts")
x <- xts::as.xts(sample_matrix)

hchart(x)

Principal Components

Each point represents one state. Axis titles give the share of variance explained by each component. Hover over a point to see the state’s name.

Use loadings = TRUE to show how the variables relate to the chosen components. Use scale = 0 for the raw observation scores.

fit <- prcomp(USArrests, scale. = TRUE)
hchart(fit, choices = c(1, 3), loadings = TRUE)

Matrix 

data(volcano)

hchart(volcano) |> # changing default color
  hc_colorAxis(
    stops = color_stops(
      colors = c(
        "#000004FF",
        "#56106EFF",
        "#BB3754FF",
        "#F98C0AFF",
        "#FCFFA4FF"
      )
    )
  )

Distance matrix 

mtcars2 <- mtcars[1:20, ]
x <- dist(mtcars2)
hchart(x)

Correlation matrix 

hchart(cor(mtcars))

GeoJSON

hchart() reads the geometry from a geo_list or geo_json FeatureCollection from geojsonio. Here the local file contains two district polygons.

library(geojsonio)

path <- system.file("extdata", "districts.geojson", package = "highcharter")
districts <- geojson_list(as.json(path))
hchart(districts)

With a mixed collection, the same call draws polygons, then lines, then points. The Maps vignette shows a clinic network with all three.
